issue.title: symvision flags monitor_records/project_records in store.py as unused, but their only consumer is intentionally accessed via module-attribute (not import) for monkeypatch compatibility

task_type_fields.impact: Blocks the symvision stage of `just check` for the whole repo -- every agent doing unrelated work anywhere in the tree hits this until it is fixed. Introduced by commit 8894213c95 "refactor(monitor): split store.py into store.py and store_lane.py". I hit it while verifying an unrelated test-file split (tests/ace/tui/test_agent_wait_resume.py) after already fixing 18 other unrelated symvision violations surfaced by other recent "toobig split" refactor commits (private-symbol-import violations in src/sase/core/disk_footprint.py and src/sase/finalizers/commit_repair.py; unused-public violations for read_continuation_json_ref in src/sase/monitor/followup_continuation.py and unexpected_remaining_paths in src/sase/finalizers/commit_validation.py, both safely made private since neither had a real external consumer). This one needs a real decision, not a mechanical rename: either find/add a sanctioned symvision escape hatch for a real in-repo Python consumer reached only via module-attribute access, revisit store_lane.py's intentional "never imported by name" design so symvision can see the usage without breaking the tests that monkeypatch sase.monitor.store.project_records, or land an upstream fix to symvision itself (per sase/memory/symvision.md we must not patch the installed package or recreate a vendored linter).
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/monitor/store.py: monitor_records() (~line 280) and project_records() (~line 343); consumed only from src/sase/monitor/store_lane.py via store.monitor_records(...) / store.project_records(...) module-attribute access
task_type_fields.repro:
Run: SASE_SYMVISION_BEAD_STATUS_ONLY=1 BD_COMMAND=tools/sase_bead .venv/bin/symvision src/sase --exclude-decorator gate_command_entrypoint --exclude-decorator builtin_chop

Reports:
  Unused public functions/classes...:
    monitor_records in src/sase/monitor/store.py
    project_records in src/sase/monitor/store.py

Both functions ARE genuinely consumed, from src/sase/monitor/store_lane.py, via `store.monitor_records(...)` / `store.project_records(...)`. store_lane.py's own module docstring (lines 1-9) explains this is deliberate: "referenced through the store module itself (never imported by name) so tests that monkeypatch sase.monitor.store.project_records (and friends) continue to control what these lookups see."

Confirmed the detection gap by contrast: store.read_monitor_marker is accessed the exact same way from store_lane.py but is NOT flagged, because it also has genuine `from sase.monitor.store import read_monitor_marker` imports elsewhere (src/sase/scripts/_agent_chat_from_name_monitor.py, src/sase/agent/running.py, src/sase/ace/scheduler/stale_running_cleanup.py, src/sase/main/monitor/show.py, src/sase/monitor/cleanup.py, and a re-export in src/sase/monitor/__init__.py) -- i.e. symvision's unused-symbol checker appears to only recognize direct `from module import name` imports as evidence of cross-file usage, not `module.attr()` attribute access.

Also confirmed the `# symvision: <ref>` pragma escape hatch does not apply: adding `# symvision: src/sase/monitor/store_lane.py` directly above each def produces `Error: symvision pragma in src/sase/monitor/store.py:280: referenced file 'src/sase/monitor/store_lane.py' is inside src/` (and the same for line 344/project_records) -- symvision explicitly rejects pragma refs that point inside src/, since it already scans that tree. So there is currently no sanctioned escape hatch for a real, visible, in-repo Python consumer that only reaches a symbol through module-attribute access.
